summary: Frontend-only retest completed for iteration 24 scope. Mobile CTA and reduced-motion flows now pass. One critical desktop regression remains: marker click does not open chapter in standard motion at 1920x1080.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking chapter marker (cars) does not trigger route/chapter open; viewport stays on circuit and Back to Circuit never appears.

integration_issues.flow: Desktop CTA -> Circuit -> marker click -> chapter open
integration_issues.issue: Marker click handler is not effectively activating chapter on desktop standard motion (hash unchanged, active state remains circuit).

action_items: Fix desktop pointer/click activation for chapter markers in standard motion mode.
Re-verify that marker click updates hash (#route-*) and sets viewport data-active to selected chapter on desktop.
Confirm Back to Circuit appears after desktop marker click opens chapter.
critical_code_review_comments: Current marker activation works via keyboard and reduced-motion paths but fails on desktop click path, suggesting pointer/click interaction mismatch rather than route-state logic failure.
Route update path should stay functionally equivalent across input modes (click/keyboard) and motion preferences.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated fixes from iteration 23: mobile 390x844 Hero CTA is visible/in-viewport/clickable and reaches circuit; reduced-motion marker click + keyboard activation + Back to Circuit all pass. Remaining blocker is desktop standard-motion marker click (cars marker) not opening chapter despite circuit state.
rca of the issue: Repro: Desktop 1920x1080 -> click Explore Legacy CTA -> wait until data-active=circuit -> click [data-testid='chapter-marker-cars']. Observed: hash remains empty and data-active remains circuit. Keyboard activation on desktop and marker click in reduced motion both work, indicating route/chapter plumbing is functional but desktop pointer click path is not reliably invoking marker activation (likely event interception or SVG click-target behavior issue in standard-motion state).
